text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Wednesday.

GERMANY - Bund futures were nearly unchanged late on Tuesday, recovering slightly from early selling linked to weak Treasuries and a technical correction to recent gains. The June Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 101.76, down 0.03 from Tuesday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts sagged on Wednesday, ending near their lows and underperforming on the way as the pound weakened, dealers said. The June long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 111-13/32, down 12/32 from Tuesday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French bond futures spent another lacklustre session tracking Bunds within a narrow range and traders predicted a similar day's trading on Thursday. The March notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 131.06 down 0.14 from Tuesday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian debt markets looked distinctly sick in late trade, with June LIF future at day's low one whole point down on day. The June bond future on LIFFE was trading at 125.73 down 1.04 from Tuesday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - US Treasury prices remained tightly range-bound around midday. The June Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 109-25/32, down 07/32 from Tuesday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.86 percent.

JAPAN - Japanese government bonds (JGBs) and futures were higher by late trade on Wednesday, supported by cash bond buying from local banks and brokers. In after hours trading the June future on LIFFE was trading at 125.81, up 0.09 from Tuesday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - Primary market activity was subdued on Wednesday, with a handful of small structured sterling bonds providing most of flows. Bankers focused on news Russia would definitely issue its mark Eurobond on Thursday. Officials at joint lead manager Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said the deal would be launched on Thursday. It would have a seven-year maturity and be for at least 1.5 billion marks. Deutsche declined to comment on other terms of the deal, but dealers elsewhere said the launch spread was likely to be between 350 and 370 b.p. over Bunds.
